XXIII.}}</noinclude>men of them, vvhich haue vowed neither to eate nor to drinke, til they kil him: and they are novv ready, expecting thy promi{{ls}}{{ls}}e. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=22}} The Tribune therfore dimi{{ls}}sed the yong man, commaunding that he {{ls}}hould {{ls}}peake to no man that he had notified the{{ls}}e things vnto him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=23}} And calling tvvo Centurions, he {{ls}}aid to them, Make ready tvvo hundred {{ls}}ouldiars, to goe as farre as Cæsaréa, and {{ls}}euentie hor{{ls}}emen, and launces tvvo hundred, from the third houre of the night: {{verse|chapter=23|verse=24}} and prepare bea{{ls}}ts. that {{ls}}etting Paul on, they might bring him {{ls}}afe to Felix the Pre{{ls}}ident {{verse|chapter=23|verse=25}} (For he feared le{{ls}}t perhaps the Ievves might take him avvay, and kil him, and him {{ls}}elf aftervvard {{ls}}hould {{ls}}u{{ls}}taine reproche, as though he vvould haue taken money) {{verse|chapter=23|verse=26}} vvriting a letter conteining this much.

''Claudius Ly{{ls}}ias to the mo{{ls}}t excellent Pre{{ls}}ident Felix, greeting''. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=27}} This man being apprehended of the Ievves, and ready to be killed of them, I comming in vvith the band deliuered him, vnder{{ls}}tanding that he is a Romane: {{verse|chapter=23|verse=28}} and meaning to know the cau{{ls}}e that they obiected vnto him, I brought him downe into their Councel. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=29}} Vvhom I found to be accu{{ls}}ed concerning que{{ls}}tions of their lavv: but hauing no crime worthie of death or of bandes. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=30}} And vvhen it vvas told me of embu{{ls}}hments that they had prepared again{{ls}}t him, I {{ls}}ent him to thee, {{ls}}ignifying al{{ls}}o to the accu{{ls}}ers, to {{ls}}peake before thee. Fare vvel. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=31}} And the {{ls}}ouldiars according as it vvas commaunded them, taking Paul, brought him by night to Antipatris. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=32}} And the next day {{ls}}ending avvay the hor{{ls}}emen to goe vvith him, they returned to the ca{{ls}}tel. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=33}} Vvho when they vvere come to Cæsaréa, and had deliuered the letter to the Pre{{ls}}ident, they did {{ls}}et Paul al{{ls}}o before him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=34}} And when he had read, and had a{{ls}}ked of vvhat prouince he vvas: and vnder{{ls}}tanding that of Cilicia: {{verse|chapter=23|verse=35}} I vvil heare the, {{ls}}aid he, vvhen thy accu{{ls}}ers are come. And he commaunded him to be kept in Herods palace.
